handoff 7.11 + 7.15. 7.15: the shared heavy-work semaphore was acquired BEFORE the first body byte and released only after the whole receive plus handler, with no read timeout -- so a client that opened a chunked upload and stalled held the slot indefinitely. Measured at cap 1: every deliverable generation, explorer render and PIR export returned 503 while one upload sat idle, and the cap scales with host RAM (1 on a <=4 GiB field laptop), making a single slow connection total denial. Acquisition moved to AFTER the body is spooled, so the slot covers the HANDLER, which is the expensive work it exists to bound. Refusing later costs only the spooled body, already capped by `limit` and discarded on return; the scope marker still prevents a second acquire and `finally` still releases exactly what was taken.
